\section[avaliar]{avaliar — to evaluate, to assess}

\label{lesson:PT-C344-avaliar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to stress, then the Portuguese for to point out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: avaliar}
\textbf{avaliar} — \textquotedblleft{}to evaluate, to assess\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O professor avalia os alunos todas as semanas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The teacher assesses the pupils every week.}
\end{quote}

Also to value: \emph{avaliar uma casa} — to value a house.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{avaliar} is built on \emph{valia} \textquotedblleft{}value, worth\textquotedblright{}, from the verb \emph{valer}, which is inherited from Latin \emph{valēre} \textquotedblleft{}to be strong, to be worth\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avaliar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avaliar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{avaliar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to stress, then the Portuguese for to point out, then say \emph{avaliar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[o juízo]{o juízo — the judgement; good sense}

\label{lesson:PT-C344-juizo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to point out, then the Portuguese for to evaluate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o juízo}
\textbf{o juízo} — \textquotedblleft{}the judgement; good sense\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ele tem pouco juízo: conduz depressa demais.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He has little sense: he drives too fast.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Ter juízo} — to be sensible; \emph{perder o juízo} — to lose your mind.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{juízo} comes from Latin \emph{iūdicium} \textquotedblleft{}a judicial investigation, a judgement\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{iūdex} \textquotedblleft{}judge\textquotedblright{}; Spanish \emph{juicio} and Italian \emph{giudizio} are its cousins (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o juízo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o juízo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o juízo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to point out, then the Portuguese for to evaluate, then say \emph{o juízo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o juízo mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The judgement; good sense\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[julgar]{julgar — to judge; to think, to believe}

\label{lesson:PT-C344-julgar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to evaluate, then the Portuguese for the judgement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: julgar}
\textbf{julgar} — \textquotedblleft{}to judge; to think, to believe\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Não é justo julgar uma pessoa pela roupa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It is not fair to judge a person by their clothes.}
\end{quote}

Also to think: \emph{julgo que sim} — I think so.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{julgar} is inherited from Latin \emph{iūdicāre} \textquotedblleft{}to judge, to pass sentence\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{iūdex} \textquotedblleft{}judge\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[objetivo]{objetivo — objective, impartial; the aim}

\label{lesson:PT-C344-objetivo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the judgement, then the Portuguese for to judge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: objetivo}
\textbf{objetivo} — \textquotedblleft{}objective, impartial; the aim\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Um juiz tem de ser objetivo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A judge has to be objective.}
\end{quote}

As a noun, \emph{o objetivo} is the aim: \emph{o meu objetivo é aprender}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{objetivo} is a learned borrowing from Medieval Latin \emph{obiectīvus} (EtymDB), built on \emph{obiectum} \textquotedblleft{}a thing set before (the mind)\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{obicere}, on \emph{iacere} \textquotedblleft{}to throw\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{objetivo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{objetivo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{objetivo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the judgement, then the Portuguese for to judge, then say \emph{objetivo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[subjetivo]{subjetivo — subjective}

\label{lesson:PT-C344-subjetivo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to judge, then the Portuguese for objective.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: subjetivo}
\textbf{subjetivo} — \textquotedblleft{}subjective\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O gosto é muito subjetivo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Taste is very subjective.}
\end{quote}

AO90 spelling; the older form was \emph{subjectivo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{subjetivo} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{subiectīvus} (EtymDB), built on \emph{subiectum} \textquotedblleft{}what lies underneath\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{subicere}, on \emph{iacere} \textquotedblleft{}to throw\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{subjetivo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{subjetivo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{subjetivo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to judge, then the Portuguese for objective, then say \emph{subjetivo} again
\end{itemize}
